judgment.rationale: The issue provides a deterministic overlap sequence and a second confirmation. Current Keyboard Manager has a complex per-shortcut started/remap state machine, making action-key overlap and pass-through suppression a focused, testable hypothesis.
evidence: With Win+Ctrl held, rapidly overlapping A and D causes unmodified A/D characters while slower alternating presses remap correctly.
The reporter explicitly narrowed the trigger to both action keys being down briefly, not raw speed.
Current KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp tracks started shortcuts, action-key key-up, and reset behavior separately across overlapping remaps.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with deterministic overlapping key events and add state-machine coverage before changing suppression logic.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix exists; the event overlap provides a concrete engine test and likely ownership boundary.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep overlapping action keys suppressed until each remap chord resolves
proposed_fixes.root_cause: When a second shortcut action key arrives while another remap with the same held modifiers is still active, the state machine can resolve one mapping and pass the other physical action key through before its own remap state is established.
plan: Create an engine test that injects Win+Ctrl down, A down, D down, A up, D up with both remaps configured.
Track suppression/ownership per physical action key rather than treating the shared modifier chord as a single active shortcut.
Release injected targets and reset each action key independently when its physical key-up arrives.
verification: Run KeyboardManagerEngine tests for overlapping Win+Ctrl+A/D remaps.
Verify slow and overlapping sequences emit only Left/Right and never literal A/D.
Cover reversed release order and auto-repeat.

confidence.rationale: The event overlap is explicit, but a current engine test is needed to confirm which reset branch leaks the second key after substantial Keyboard Manager changes.

issue_context.summary: Two remapped shortcuts sharing held modifiers can leak the second action key when the next chord begins before the first action key is fully released.
known_information: The exact mappings and event sequence are documented.
The failure depends on A and D overlapping while Win+Ctrl remain held.
A second user reproduced the same behavior with Ctrl+A/Ctrl+E remaps.
inferences: Shortcut state is likely being reset at chord scope rather than preserving independent ownership for simultaneously held action keys.
issue_context.analysis: The original report already contains the key discriminator. A synthetic low-level input test can reproduce this without asking the reporter for generic logs.

reproduce.title: Replay overlapping Keyboard Manager chords
prerequisites: Configure Win+Ctrl+A → Left and Win+Ctrl+D → Right
Open a text editor containing text
steps: Press A down, then D down before releasing A.
Release A, then D; repeat with the release order reversed.
Inspect both resulting cursor movement and low-level emitted key events.
reproduce.expected_result: Only Left and Right are emitted; no literal A or D reaches the editor and all modifiers release normally.
